Question: If I've done 4 years of graduation from Pakistan, Can I study Bachelor's again in the US or a European Country? The main reason is that IELTS requirements are higher for master's programs. Also, I want to change my field of study, is it possible?
Answer: Absolutely, if you can afford the $30,000 or more a year it will cost to pursue a bachelor’s degree in the US. And that’s not for an institution you have ever heard of or located in a place that will interest you. That’s an approximate baseline of the lowest cost you will find. Most institutions will be more expensive. There are not scholarships or aid for students pursuing a second degree (and they’re quite rare for students pursuing a first degree).

Question: What do you think would have been the "best alternative" or the least damaging alternative for Alan Turing after his 1952 trial which was a dead end: prison or the harmful chemical castration he eventually underwent?
Answer: While as a concept it's horrifying and I would never defend it, I think your framing is a bit dramatic. Turing was placed on DES for one year, during which he experienced both a loss of libido and some unpleasant body changes. However, this is often cited as a primary motive for his suicide. There are a couple of problems with that. First, while the inquest concluded suicide, there was no note and there are reasonable explanations for how Turing came to accidentally ingest suicide (he was working with it in his research and had been for a while). We will never know one way or the other. Second, he had been off of DES for over a year when he died. The obvious solution is to decriminalize homosexuality, and that did happen, even if not in time to prevent Turing from coming to harm. What would have happened had Turing not accepted the chemical castration treatment and instead was sent to prison? We can't possibly know.

Question: Is it possible to survive with a PhD stipend in Canada?
Answer: Canada is a big country with absurdly expensive big cities, expensive moderate sized cities, more affordable moderate sized cities, and reasonably affordable small cities. There may be some other variants in there, too. However, Canada produces a significant number of PhD each year, so the basic answer is “yes”. A more specific answer depends on the city where you will be living in, the stipend amount itself, and your needs. A single person who doesn’t mind having roommates is in a radically different financial position than a married person supporting a spouse and children.

Question: Why do companies make you sign up for job apps like indeed? Is this just a scam so they can have your information in some way and get ads and PO-up in your email? Also would they use this like a blacklist to tell other companies about you?
Answer: No. It’s because the system works in their favor; you want a job, they have the job, and so you’ll use a system that’s convenient for them. And the alternative, which isn’t uncommon, is to create a separate account on the corporate system for each company you’re applying for and re-enter all of your data. That’s not more convenient for you. Also, a blacklist or blocklist or whatever you want to call it is a list of people, companies, etc., who are off limits. But you know who does sell information about you and everything you do? And who knows who you are, even if you think that they don’t and you didn’t tell them? Quora. And every other social media site you use.

Question: How can I get into UC Berkeley for a master’s in CS as a bachelor mathematics student at UIO from Norway?
Answer: It’s a very competitive program. It’s also primarily designed for students who want to get into PhD programs (so it has strong research emphasis). So getting in is straightforward: just be an incredibly competitive candidate and get lucky. Straightforward is not the same as easy. The UC Berkeley MS CS is a stretch/reach program for ALL candidates. It should be one of several programs you apply to, and there should be less-competitive programs in the list, too.
